newsitem.title: USA: LifeCell says AlloDerm does well in study.
newsitem.headline: LifeCell says AlloDerm does well in study.

text.p: LifeCell Corp said on Friday that a study found its AlloDerm skin-graft product to be beneficial in the reconstruction of burn wounds.
AlloDerm also has been found useful when used as an initial, permanent dermal graft for elderly patients, the company said.

Dr. D.A. Reilly of the University of California at Davis used AlloDerm together with ultra-thin autografts on seven burn patients with 14 burn-wound contracture complications. The successful engraftment rate for AlloDerm was 90 percent, LifeCell said.
The company said AlloDerm was found to reduce wound-contracture complications, which are a long-term complication of third-degree burns.
LifeCell also said a study at the Burn Center of the Medical College of Virginia found that AlloDerm may be helpful when used as the initial graft for full-thickness burn wounds in elderly patients.
AlloDerm also is used in plastic, reconstructive and periodontal surgery.
